body:
Periodic resource, guard and clear gradient propagation now runs on one background worker by default and publishes eight ticks after seeding. This overlaps the main simulation without scheduling extra refreshes. After rebasing onto the kernel optimization in #391, the retained six-scenario screen measured 1.207× aggregate wall speedup with 0.5% more whole-process CPU against the same eight-tick serial schedule (worst heavy-scenario CPU increase 1.5%). The earlier kernel measured 1.252× with 2.4% more CPU; additional workers offered little consistent benefit.

The main thread seeds fields at the existing round-robin boundary. Workers use private fields, scratch storage and frozen terrain. Results publish only at the fixed deadline, waiting if late and discarding snapshots superseded by synchronous refreshes. Buffers are bounded by the delay. Worker creation failure and browser builds use the same delayed serial schedule.

Saving completes private work without publishing early and records pending fields, destinations, supersession flags and remaining deadlines. Reloading preserves this state; worker count is local execution configuration. Headless `--gradient-workers 0` provides the identical-schedule serial control. Replay headers are written after headless scheduling configuration so experimental delays are reproduced too.

Compatibility and feel:
- Save format 120 adds pending gradients with version-gated loading; the save floor remains 58. Existing saves remain loadable and start with an empty queue.
- Replay floor 120 and network protocol 43 reject incompatible routing schedules. Old replay playback is intentionally no longer supported.
- Periodic routing fields can be eight ticks older, which can change decisions, pacing and game outcomes. Synchronous refreshes remain immediate. The maintainer explicitly approved the default behavior in the task conversation.
- No AI observation or policy changes. The earlier blocking area/initialization/hiring experiments remain selectable controls with equivalence tests. A narrow Castor initialization fix prevents allocator contents entering saved telemetry.

Validation:
- Release build; scheduler ThreadSanitizer, failures/fallback, fixed deadlines, cancellation, bounded storage, teardown and snapshot/restore at every delay phase.
- Real resource/guard/clear supersession and frozen-terrain tests; 2,032,787-cell independent path oracle.
- Exact per-tick traces at delays 1/3/8 across 0/1/2/4/8 workers. Real-game save continuation at all eight phases across 0/1/2 workers; binary/text runtime-state round trips; malformed queue rejection.
- Blocking experiment matrix preserves replay/save bytes and continuation. Echo/Maxima repeated save continuation and replay/network acceptance-boundary tests pass locally.
- Committed reference traces generated with zero workers and matched byte-for-byte with one worker let Linux and Windows CI verify the same legacy starting saves against macOS results. All reference traces still match after the #391 rebase. Linux and Windows CI passed the exact macOS reference comparisons on this engine revision.

Performance evidence: eight-tick/one-worker screen used one warmup and two measured repetitions over six 64–512 map scenarios. Three-tick confirmation and a complete 82,402-tick game received five repetitions. Measurements used an Apple M3 with other simulation workloads running; the 1.5× target was not met. Game-length changes are excluded from threading speedup claims. Full-engine ThreadSanitizer is not established because the local SDL initializer blocked before main; the standalone scheduler passes.

Supersedes #212, with credit to Giszmo for the background-gradient approach and original measurements. That PR has been closed and linked here.

Reviewable evidence: [benchmark fixtures, measurements, complete-game trace and default validation logs](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/evidence/gradient-pipeline-390).

The branch is rebased on `de84ffc18` (#391), retaining its flat 64-bucket kernel and resource-seeding optimization with private worker storage. Rebased validation and timing rows are in `rebase-validation.tar.gz` on the evidence branch.

Additional 3/4/5/6/7/8-tick screen completed across all six scenarios, with exact serial/thread trace checks for the new intermediate delays. Host contention affected the final scenario, so neighboring delays cannot be reliably ranked; 5–8 ticks largely plateau and eight had the lowest summed deadline wait. Keeping eight ticks. [Full table, caveats and raw rows](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/evidence/gradient-pipeline-390/delay-results.md). The Maxima army-birth oracle was regenerated with serial eight-tick publication and verified with the default worker; the complete Maxima suite passes locally.

CI note: the self-hosting deployment job inherited from #392 fails with HTTP 404 because the split `web-deploy` job neither builds nor downloads the WebAssembly assets required by `tests/deployment/test_compose.py`. Its workflow and deployment code are unchanged by this PR. [Failure log](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/actions/runs/36521066641/job/109253813957). Windows engine validation passed, including the exact macOS reference checksums. Linux passed the Maxima suite, save portability/continuation, gradient oracle and cross-platform checksum checks. Android builds passed. The final commit only refreshes the browser replay fixture to format 120: both affected import/reload tests passed locally against the CI-built WebAssembly artifact, as did replay saving and the 1,500-tick native/WebAssembly comparison (SHA-256 `9368bcbec9b2f29bc44e9f40bff3776985283aad6a29f3c5ad9bfc06d37b36b8`). The full CI rerun for that fixture-only commit is still pending; these results do not claim an entirely green final-head workflow.
title: Pipeline periodic gradients by default with one worker and eight-tick publication
